# Model selection (corrective action CA3) {#sec-selection}

## Procedure {#sec-sel-procedure}

Model selection was adopted as corrective action CA3 on `{python} sel_date`, before INV-001 closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. It replaced the analysis of every output, the refits of corrective action CA2 included. Each report with a response-surface design applies it to every output of the design, on all runs in which the output was measured. Where a design was augmented, the planned runs form the first block and the augmentation runs the second. The verification of the platform worst cases behind the intermediate acceptance criteria applies the same procedure (@sec-sel-verification). PCMP-001 is not changed. Each report records the model selection as a discrepancy from its plan (@sec-impact). The procedure has four steps:

1. The scale. The Box-Cox profile likelihood of the power λ is calculated for the full quadratic model of the output, with the block term where the runs form two blocks [@boxcox1964]. The output is modelled on the log scale (λ = 0) where the 95 % profile-likelihood interval of λ contains 0 and excludes 1. Otherwise it is modelled on the raw scale (λ = 1). The rule chooses between these two scales only. Where the interval excludes both 0 and 1, as for `{python} excl_both_phrase`, the raw scale is kept. Only an output whose results are all positive can take the log scale.
2. The search. Every submodel of the full quadratic model that respects strong hierarchy is fitted on that scale. Strong hierarchy allows an interaction only together with both of its main effects, and a squared term only together with its main effect. The block term is kept in every candidate. The candidate with the lowest AICc is selected (@sec-sel-search). An output that the data give without error, with replicates that agree exactly at the precision the method reports, is fitted exactly by more than one candidate. AICc is not defined for an exact fit, so the smallest candidate that fits exactly is selected instead. `{python} exact_txt`
3. The check. The selected model is judged against PCMP-001 §7.2 on its own scale, by the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting. A selected model with terms must also have a significant model F-test at α = `{python} eff_a_s`. Only the selected model is judged. If it fails, no other candidate takes its place. The selection used the same runs that §7.2 then judges. A model chosen as the best of many candidates fits those runs better than a model fixed in advance, so §7.2 is an optimistic check of a selected model. @sec-sel-aug gives the one independent check that exists.
4. The offset. The scale-down offset of an output is taken on the scale of its model, with its `{python} f"{100 * ci_off:.0f}"` % confidence interval. For a raw-scale output it is the mean of the scale-down set-point runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, and it is subtracted from a scale-down prediction. For a log-scale output it is the same difference of the mean logarithms, reported as a ratio of geometric means, and a scale-down prediction is divided by it.

The check has three outcomes. A selected model with terms that passes is the predictive model of the output, and it sets the ranges of its step. A selected model with no term passes when it meets the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting. It says that no effect of the parameters was detected within the range studied, at the power the design gives (@sec-ss-power). It does not show that there is none. For a model of the mean alone, R² is zero and R² minus predicted R² depends on the number of runs only, `{python} f2(gap_mean_only(n_lo))` for `{python} n_lo` runs and `{python} f2(gap_mean_only(n_hi))` for `{python} n_hi`, so for such a model the check reduces to the lack-of-fit test. An output whose selected model fails has no adequate model. It is judged on its measured results, as @sec-rule describes, and it sets no range.

## Why a log scale, and what it changes {#sec-sel-log}

Host cell protein in the Protein A pool shows what the log scale does. On the log scale the selected model has the form

$$\ln y = b_0 + b_1 x_1 + b_2 x_2 + \dots + \varepsilon$$

and, transformed back,

$$y = e^{b_0} \cdot e^{b_1 x_1} \cdot e^{b_2 x_2} \cdots e^{\varepsilon}$$

Here y is pool host cell protein in `{python} hcp_unit`, x₁, x₂ and so on are the parameters in coded units, from −1 at the low end of the range studied to +1 at the high end, and ε is the error of a single run. Each parameter multiplies the output by a fixed factor, $e^{b}$ per coded unit and $e^{2b}$ from the low to the high end of its range. The error multiplies it too, so the scatter in `{python} hcp_unit` grows with the level. Across the range studied, the selected model multiplies pool host cell protein by a factor of `{python} fold_txt`, from the low to the high end of each parameter. A factor below one is a decrease. `{python} cap1(sq_h_txt)` also has a squared term, so its effect is not the same along its range.

Two properties of the process and the method make host cell protein behave this way. A purification step removes a share of what is present, so a parameter changes the share that is removed, not a fixed amount. The precision of the host cell protein ELISA (`{python} elisa["id"]`) is a percentage of the level, `{python} f"{elisa['precision_pct']:g}"` %, so the scatter of the results grows with the level. Effects that multiply look like an interaction when they are added on the raw scale. On the raw scale the full quadratic model needs the interaction `{python} int_h_txt` (`{python} ptxt(p_int_raw)`). On the log scale the same interaction is not significant (`{python} ptxt(p_int_log)`), and the selected model has no interaction at all.

Least squares, and the t-tests, F-tests and prediction intervals built on it, assume residuals that are independent and normally distributed, with mean zero and the same variance over the whole range studied. On the raw scale the full quadratic model of pool host cell protein has a residual SD of `{python} f"{sd_raw_lo:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` in the lower half of its predictions and `{python} f"{sd_raw_hi:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit` in the upper half. On the log scale the same model has `{python} f"{sd_log_lo:.3f}"` and `{python} f"{sd_log_hi:.3f}"`, in natural-log units. The upper half is `{python} f"{sd_raw_ratio:.2f}"` times the lower on the raw scale and `{python} f"{sd_log_ratio:.2f}"` times on the log scale. The Box-Cox profile puts λ at `{python} f2(bc_h["lambda"])`, with a 95 % interval from `{python} num_txt(bc_h["lo"], 2)` to `{python} num_txt(bc_h["hi"], 2)`, which contains 0 and excludes 1. The assumption of equal variance holds on the log scale and does not hold on the raw scale.

The log scale changes the following, and nothing else:

1. The criterion stays in its own unit, `{python} hcp_unit`, and the prediction limits are transformed back into it.
2. Effects are fold changes, as above.
3. The scale-down offset is a ratio of geometric means, `{python} f2(off_h["offset"])` for pool host cell protein with a `{python} f"{100 * off_h['ci']:.0f}"` % confidence interval from `{python} f2(off_h["lo"])` to `{python} f2(off_h["hi"])`, and a scale-down prediction is divided by it.
4. A prediction interval is calculated on the log scale and transformed back. It keeps its 95 % coverage, because the probability that ln y lies between two values is the probability that y lies between their antilogs. It is therefore suitable, and the least-squares assumption behind it holds on the log scale, which on the raw scale it does not.
5. The interval is asymmetric, further above the predicted value than below it. At the least favourable combination of the NOR (`{python} wc_h_txt`), the predicted pool host cell protein is `{python} f"{wc_h['predicted']:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit`, and the 95 % prediction interval of a single run runs from `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_low']:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_high']:,.0f}"` `{python} hcp_unit`, `{python} f"{wc_h['predicted'] - wc_h['pi_low']:,.0f}"` below and `{python} f"{wc_h['pi_high'] - wc_h['predicted']:,.0f}"` above.
6. The predicted value is the median of the output, its geometric mean, not its arithmetic mean. The upper prediction limit, which is judged against an upper criterion, is not affected by that.
7. Near an upper criterion, where the level is high, a raw-scale model understates the scatter, because it pools one residual SD over all levels. The interval from the log scale is correctly wider there.

In the reports, `{python} n_log_sel` of the `{python} n_models` outputs with a criterion are modelled on the log scale. They are `{python} log_sel_phrase`.

## How the model is searched {#sec-sel-search}

The goal of the search is the model with the lowest AICc among all hierarchical submodels of the full quadratic. AICc estimates how well a model would predict new runs. It rewards a close fit and charges a penalty for every estimated quantity, so that a term is kept only where it improves the fit by more than its penalty [@hurvich1989; @burnham2002]. AICc is Akaike's criterion, AIC, with a correction for small samples. The correction raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as in these designs, so that the criterion does not favour models with too many terms. For the full quadratic model on `{python} n4` runs, AIC charges `{python} aic_pen` for its `{python} K_full` estimated quantities (`{python} k4` coefficients and the residual variance), and the correction adds `{python} f"{aicc_corr:.1f}"` to that.

The search fits every candidate, `{python} f"{n_cand[4]:,}"` for a design with four factors, `{python} n_cand[3]` for three and `{python} n_cand[2]` for two, the model of the mean included. It takes the candidate with the lowest AICc. The candidates are listed in a fixed order, from the fewest main effects upward, and a tie goes to the first. A stepwise search, by contrast, adds or removes one term at a time and stops when no single change lowers AICc. It therefore stops where only a combination of changes would lower AICc further.

On this campaign's data the two searches were compared for `{python} n_cmp` outputs with a criterion. The output that fits exactly has no AICc and is left out. A backward stepwise search from the full quadratic would have stopped at a model with a higher AICc than the best candidate for `{python} n_bw` of them, a forward search from the mean for `{python} n_fw`, and one or the other for `{python} n_either`. For `{python} attr_prose(EXK[1], EXK[0])` `{python} at_step(EXK[0])`, for example, the exhaustive search selects `{python} int(ex.n_terms)` terms with an AICc of `{python} num_txt(ex.aicc)`. A backward search stops at `{python} int(ex.backward_terms)` terms (`{python} num_txt(ex.backward_aicc)`) and a forward search at `{python} int(ex.forward_terms)` terms (`{python} num_txt(ex.forward_aicc)`).

The backward elimination of corrective action CA2 differed from this search in three ways. It was stepwise. It decided by p-value, which tests each term against zero and does not compare models. It also worked on the raw scale only.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-sel-verification}

PCMP-001 Version 2.0 derives the intermediate acceptance criteria a priori. Each drug substance criterion is carried back through the platform worst case of every downstream step, its lowest clearance fold or its largest increase, and each platform worst case is the result of a single run. The verification of these worst cases uses the same model selection, on the planned runs of each downstream step. For each worst case it predicts the output of the step at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the NOR as characterized. At each combination it also takes the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch, on the scale of the model and transformed back. Both are converted into a clearance fold or an increase, and the least favourable value over the combinations is the bound of the step.

Where the predicted value of a step is worse than the platform worst case, the bound replaces the platform value, and the criteria upstream of the step tighten. Where the bound itself is better than the platform worst case, on a selected model that meets §7.2, the bound replaces the platform value, and the criteria upstream widen. Otherwise the platform value stays. Both directions use the single-batch bound, never a confidence bound of the mean, because every output is judged per batch and the platform worst case that the bound replaces was a single run. A bound from a tolerance interval would be statistically purer, but it is too conservative, and the single-batch prediction bound was chosen as the pragmatic rule. The bound is pointwise at each combination, not simultaneous over them.

A replacement does not always mean that the product did better. The platform worst cases of the low-pH hold are increases over a hold of `{python} plat_hold` min, while the A-Mab value is the increase within the NOR as characterized, which allows at most `{python} nor_hold_max` min. Where the A-Mab increase replaces the platform value, the replacement reflects the shorter hold, not a more stable product. The criterion that follows is still right, because routine manufacture never holds longer than the NOR. @sec-impact-criteria gives the criteria that the bounds of the selected models changed, and the risk of each change.

## What model selection changed {#sec-sel-changed}

Model selection gives an adequate model for `{python} n_sel_ok` of the `{python} n_models` outputs with a criterion. Every output whose full quadratic model met §7.2 has an adequate selected model. Of the `{python} n_fail` outputs whose full quadratic model failed, `{python} n_fail_ok` have an adequate selected model and `{python} n_none_sel` have none. @tbl-impact gives the model of each output in the report of its step.

### The augmentations {#sec-sel-aug}

The three models that the augmentations were made for meet §7.2 on the planned runs alone once they are selected. They are the models of high mannose and acidic variants at the production bioreactor and of host cell protein at anion exchange. The augmentations were therefore not needed to pass that test. They were decided on `{python} decided` under the model of the plan, the full quadratic, which failed §7.2 on the planned runs. Both started before model selection was adopted on `{python} sel_date`. The anion exchange runs were still under way on that date, as were the production bioreactor runs, and both were completed.

@tbl-sharpen gives the three selected models on the planned runs and on all runs, with all three statistics of §7.2. Each meets §7.2 on both sets of runs. For high mannose, `{python} len(AUG[HM]["dropped"])` terms of the model selected on the planned runs are not in the model selected on all runs. These are `{python} hm_dropped`. On all runs the selected model of high mannose is on the log scale and has `{python} len(AUG[HM]["sel_a"]["names"])` terms (`{python} hm_all`). The scale changed with the second block as well, so part of the change in terms may come from the scale. For acidic variants every term of the model selected on the planned runs is kept on all runs, and the second block resolves `{python} len(AUG[AV]["added"])` further terms (`{python} av_added`). For host cell protein at anion exchange the selected model is the same on both sets of runs. It has the main effects of `{python} hcp_terms`, on the log scale.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sh_tbl, "Selected models of the outputs that the augmentations were made for, on the planned runs and on all runs.",
        "tbl-sharpen", merge=["Step", "Attribute"], header=sh_head, align=sh_align, notes=sh_notes,
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

Passing §7.2 on the planned runs did not make every model reliable. @tbl-aug-check tests each model selected on the planned runs of the two augmented steps against the augmentation runs, which it has not seen. If a model is right, about 95 % of the new runs fall inside its 95 % prediction interval, and its prediction error is close to its own residual SD. High mannose and aggregates at the production bioreactor predict the new runs worst. Only `{python} int(hm_c.inside_pi)` and `{python} int(agg_c.inside_pi)` of `{python} int(hm_c.n_new)` fall inside the interval, and the prediction error is `{python} f"{hm_c.ratio:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{agg_c.ratio:.1f}"` times the residual SD of the model. For the other outputs the ratio is at most `{python} f"{others_ratio:.1f}"`. The block term is not significant for any output on all runs (the smallest p-value is `{python} f"{block_p_min:.3f}"`), so the misses come from the models, not from a shift between the blocks.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(apc_tbl, "Prediction of the augmentation runs by the models selected on the planned runs.", "tbl-aug-check",
        merge=["Step"], header=apc_head, align=apc_align, notes=apc_notes, notes_per_row=True,
        size="footnotesize").show()
```

On all runs, high mannose loses the interactions `{python} hm_int_txt` that the planned runs suggested. Aggregates lose the terms `{python} agg_drop_txt` and gain a curvature in `{python} agg_add_txt.replace("²", "")`. The augmentation was not needed to pass the test, but it changed what these two models say, and the reports use the models of all runs. For acidic variants the model selected on the planned runs predicts every new run within its interval, and the model of all runs adds the terms that the second block resolves.

### Outputs with no adequate model {#sec-sel-none}

After selection, `{python} n_none_sel` outputs have no adequate model. They are `{python} none_sel_phrase`. Each is judged on its measured results, which is a weaker standard than the prediction interval of a single future batch that a modelled output meets (@sec-rule). @tbl-measured gives each criterion, the most adverse measured result and the margin between them. Every measured result meets its criterion. None of these outputs sets a range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(mr_tbl, "Outputs with no adequate model, judged on their measured results.", "tbl-measured",
        header=mr_head, align=mr_align, notes=mr_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The fragment models `{python} none_frag_txt` had no adequate refit under corrective action CA2 either. XMuLV clearance at virus filtration is the one output for which model selection and the refit by backward elimination disagree on whether an adequate model exists. The refit had reduced it to its mean, which meets §7.2. Model selection keeps a term in `{python} vf_terms`, because that model has the lower AICc (`{python} num_txt(fv["aicc"])` against `{python} num_txt(aicc_mean_vf)` for the mean alone). Only the selected model is judged. Its model F-test is not significant (`{python} ptxt(fv["p"])`), and its R² minus predicted R² of `{python} f2(fv["gap"])` exceeds the limit of `{python} gap_max_s`. XMuLV clearance at virus filtration is therefore judged on its measured results. The two models differ by `{python} f"{d_aicc_vf:.1f}"` in AICc. Models within two units of each other have about equal support [@burnham2002], so the outcome for this output rests on a small difference.

### An output that fits exactly

`{python} cap1(out_phrase(exact_sel))` fit exactly. The replicates returned the same value to the precision the method reports. There is therefore no pure error to test lack of fit against, and the model reproduces every run. The smallest model that fits exactly is taken, with `{python} exact_terms` as its only term.

### Outputs with no detected effect

The selected models of `{python} n_zero_sel` outputs have no term. They are `{python} zero_sel_phrase`. No effect of the parameters on them was detected within the ranges studied, at the power the designs give (@sec-ss-power). The model is their mean, with the block term where the design has two blocks.

### The criteria and the scale-down qualifications

The intermediate acceptance criteria rest on the verification with the selected models (@sec-sel-verification). Model selection made `{python} n_cd` of them wider. Against the criteria that the full quadratic models would have given, the scale-down model would not be qualified for host cell protein in the Protein A pool or at cation exchange. In both cases the low end of the offset interval decides. The upper prediction limit over the NOR would then be `{python} f"{QD[HK]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]` against a criterion of `{python} f"{QD[HK]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]` in the Protein A pool, and `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` against `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]` at cation exchange. These two qualifications rest on the widening, which @sec-impact-criteria sets out.

# Impact assessment {#sec-impact}

The investigation changes the model of every output with a criterion in the report of its step. @tbl-impact lists the outputs by report. For each output it gives the remedy that the rule gave a failing full quadratic model, the model that the report uses after model selection, and the discrepancies from the plan that the report records.

        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()

Each report records the augmentation and the model selection as discrepancies from its plan, identified as plan discrepancies (PD). A discrepancy from the plan records work or an analysis that the approved plan did not foresee. A deviation records a departure from a procedure or a GMP requirement. No procedure and no GMP requirement was departed from, so neither is recorded as a deviation. The production bioreactor report (`{python} rep["bioreactor"]`) records the production bioreactor augmentation as `{python} pd_id["bioreactor"]`, and the anion exchange report (`{python} rep["aex"]`) records the anion exchange augmentation as `{python} pd_id["aex"]`. Each of the `{python} n_steps` reports with a response-surface design records the model selection (`{python} sel_pd_txt`). PCMP-001 and the plans are not amended.

## Acceptance criteria {#sec-impact-criteria}

Model selection was adopted on `{python} sel_date`, before INV-001 closed on `{python} INV["closed"]` and fixed the intermediate acceptance criteria. The verification of the platform worst cases behind the criteria in force therefore used the selected models of the planned runs (@sec-sel-verification). The same verification on the full quadratic models, the analysis the plans prescribed, gives different values for `{python} n_cd` criteria. Model selection made all `{python} n_cd` wider, by `{python} pct_txt`. @tbl-criteria-ca3 lists them, with the downstream worst cases whose values differ between the two verifications.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.CTable(header=crit_head, body=crit_body, caption="Intermediate acceptance criteria that differ between the verification on the full quadratic models and on the selected models.",
         label="tbl-criteria-ca3", align=crit_align, notes=crit_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The differences come from changes at `{python} n_change_steps` downstream steps:

1. Anion exchange. The full quadratic model of host cell protein does not meet §7.2, so its bound of `{python} b_aex_f` cannot widen a criterion, and the platform worst-case clearance fold of `{python} p_aex` enters the derivation. The selected model meets §7.2, and its bound of `{python} b_aex_s` replaces the platform fold. The host cell protein criteria `{python} hcp_crit_txt` therefore widen, because both lie upstream of anion exchange.
2. Cation exchange. The selected model of aggregate is on the log scale with `{python} n_terms_cxa` terms, and it gives a different prediction and a different single-batch bound from the full quadratic model. The predicted aggregate fold is worse than the platform fold on both models, so the bound replaces it on both. It tightens the aggregate criteria `{python} agg_crit_txt`, which lie upstream of cation exchange, by a different amount on each model. For host cell protein the predicted fold meets the platform fold of `{python} p_cexh` on both models and its single-batch bound does not, so the platform fold stays on both, and no criterion moves because of host cell protein at cation exchange.
3. Low-pH viral inactivation. The single-batch bound of the aggregate increase is better than the platform value on both models, differs slightly between them, and enters the production bioreactor criterion. This replacement reflects the shorter hold of the NOR as characterized, at most `{python} nor_hold_max` min against the `{python} plat_hold`-min hold of the platform worst case, not a more stable product.

Each widening rests on the one-sided `{python} vb_pct` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination of the NOR as characterized, from a selected model that meets §7.2. A §7.2 check of a selected model is optimistic (@sec-sel-procedure), so @tbl-ca3-sensitivity shows what depends on the widening. Judged against the criteria that the full quadratic models would have given, no output changes its conclusion over the NOR in force. One proven acceptable range moves. For host cell protein in the Protein A pool, the lower end of the `{python} pname(HK[0], PF)` range moves from `{python} f"{par_in[PF][0]:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{par_wo[PF][0]:.2f}"`, and both lie below the NOR of `{python} f"{pf_nor[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{pf_nor[1]:g}"`.

Two qualifications of a scale-down model do depend on the widening. A scale-down model is qualified for an output when its conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} f"{100 * ci_off:.0f}"` % confidence interval (PCMP-001). Against the criteria without model selection, the scale-down model would not be qualified for host cell protein in the Protein A pool or at cation exchange. In both cases the low end of the offset interval decides. In the Protein A pool, with the offset at the low end of its interval, a ratio of `{python} f2(QD[HK]["off"]["lo"])`, the upper 95 % prediction limit over the NOR at manufacturing scale is `{python} f"{QD[HK]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]`. That is above the criterion of `{python} f"{QD[HK]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]` that the full quadratic models give, and below the criterion in force of `{python} f"{QD[HK]['crit_in']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[HK]["unit"]`. At cation exchange, with the offset at `{python} f2(QD[CXH]["off"]["lo"])`, the same limit is `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['lim_lo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]`, against `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['crit_wo']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]` without model selection and `{python} f"{QD[CXH]['crit_in']:,.0f}"` `{python} QD[CXH]["unit"]` in force. These two qualifications rest on the criteria that model selection widened.

Each change that model selection made is argued by its risk. The criteria concern host cell protein and aggregates, which are attributes of the drug substance specification, with limits of `{python} ds_txt`. An excursion at a step is therefore detected at drug substance release, where both are tested. A step output at its criterion still gives a drug substance within its limit, as long as each downstream step clears at least the value that the derivation uses. For host cell protein these are a fold of `{python} p_cexh` at cation exchange, the platform worst case, and `{python} b_aex_s` at anion exchange, its single-batch bound. For aggregates they are a fold of `{python} g3(cexa_fold_in)` at cation exchange and an increase of `{python} g3(via_add_in)` % at low-pH viral inactivation, both single-batch bounds. The integrated process model gives no out-of-specification drug substance for either attribute in its `{python} f"{n_mc_poos:,}"` simulated batches, and a normal-tail probability of less than one per million. The risk of the wider criteria therefore falls on the producer, as a batch that fails release, and not on the patient.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(sens_tbl, "What depends on the criteria that model selection widened.", "tbl-ca3-sensitivity",
        header=sens_head, align=sens_align, notes=sens_notes, notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

The augmentation runs moved no criterion. Both augmentations ended after INV-001 closed, on `{python} aug_end_txt`, and the verification uses only the planned runs of each step. Repeated on all runs of anion exchange, the verification gives the same bound for host cell protein, `{python} f"{b_aex_all:.3g}"`, so the augmentation runs would not have moved the criteria either.

## Conclusions over the NOR {#sec-impact-nor}

The conclusion over the NOR of an output does not depend on the choice between the full quadratic model of the planned runs and the model that the report uses. For every output with a criterion the two give the same conclusion, at the NOR as characterized and at the NOR in force. Two of these conclusions are not met on either model, and both rested on full quadratic models that fail §7.2:

1. XMuLV clearance at low-pH viral inactivation is judged on the mean LRF at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions (PCMP-001 §6.4). The criterion is the platform claim of the step, `{python} f"{claim6:g}"` log10. The claims of the three viral clearance steps add up to `{python} f"{vcum.claimed_sum:g}"` log10, against a cumulative requirement of `{python} f"{vcum.required:g}"` log10. The selected model has the main effects of `{python} fit6_terms` only. On it, the lowest mean LRF within the NOR as characterized is `{python} f2(y6.min())`, at `{python} worst6`, so the step claim is not met. The full quadratic model gives a lowest mean of `{python} f2(y6f.min())` and the same conclusion. The low-pH viral inactivation report (`{python} rep[vk]`) moves the NOR of `{python} moved6_txt`, and it states the conclusion over the NOR in force.
2. Acidic variants at the production bioreactor are judged on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The lower limit of the criterion is `{python} f"{av_floor:g}"` %, the lower limit of the drug substance specification carried to the step unchanged. On the selected model of all runs, the lower prediction limit at `{python} worst_b` is `{python} f"{av_lo:.1f}"` % at manufacturing scale, so the criterion is not met. The predicted median at the same settings is `{python} f"{av_med:.1f}"` %, `{python} av_med_word` the criterion. On the full quadratic model of the planned runs the lower prediction limit at the same settings is `{python} f"{avc_full['pi_low']:.1f}"` %, and the criterion is not met either. The production bioreactor report (`{python} rep[bk]`) states how this result is handled.

`{python} cap1(none_sel_phrase)` have no adequate model and are judged on their measured results (@tbl-measured).

## Other documents

The other documents of the package are affected as follows:

1. INV-001, the investigation into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen, is not reopened. Its comparison of the Version 1.0 and Version 2.0 criteria uses the models that Version 1.0 fitted, so that it shows what the change of criteria moved.
2. PCMP-001 §7.2 leaves it to the investigation of a failing model to state when a design is augmented and how the number of runs is calculated. PCMP-001 is not changed for model selection, which each report records as a discrepancy from its plan.
3. The process characterization master report (PCMR-001) consolidates the conclusions of the step reports after the remedies and the model selection.

The investigation has no product impact. No batch was dispositioned on these models, and the Version 1.0 documents were on hold for BLA use.

# Corrective and preventive actions {#sec-capa}

@tbl-capa lists the corrective and preventive actions. Model selection, corrective action CA3, replaced the refits by backward elimination of corrective action CA2 in the reports, so CA2 stands as the record of how the rule was applied. Corrective action CA1, the augmentation of the designs that the rule names, has two parts. Its augmentation runs were complete at closure. Its second part, the re-evaluation of the augmented designs on all runs, is carried by the Version 2.0 reports of the two steps, due on `{python} capa.loc["CA1", "due"]`, together with the models chosen by model selection.

Preventive action PA1, the design-size check, checks each new design by simulation before its plan is approved, at the expected effects and with the analysis the plan states. The simulation of @sec-sample-size used the full quadratic model, the analysis the Version 1.0 plans prescribed. Preventive action PA2 revises SOP-1002, the procedure for the `{python} sop1002`, so that a plan states its model-selection procedure.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(capa_tbl, "Corrective and preventive actions of INV-002.", "tbl-capa",
        align=["P{0.9cm}", "P{8.6cm}", "P{1.7cm}", "P{1.9cm}", "P{2.6cm}"],
        size="footnotesize").show()
```

# Effectiveness check {#sec-effectiveness}

The actions are checked for effectiveness by `{python} EFFECTIVENESS2["due"]`. The criterion is `{python} EFFECTIVENESS2["criterion"]`. The design-size check is the simulation of preventive action PA1. For each planned model it gives the probability of meeting the model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2, and from these the number of planned models expected to fail, with an upper 95 % limit.

# Conclusion and closure {#sec-closure}

The investigation confirmed the classification as `{python} INV2["classification"]`, on the grounds recorded when it was opened: `{python} class_basis`. No range was set from a failing model at Version 2.0.

The root cause is that the plans prescribed the full quadratic model as the predictive model, with no model selection, on designs that are small for it. The Version 1.0 plans set no adequacy criterion against which the size of a design could have been checked. A remedy was assigned to every failing model by a rule approved before any new run, and both augmentations were run by `{python} last_end`. Model selection then replaced the refits for every output. Once selected, the models that the augmentations were made for meet §7.2 on the planned runs alone. The augmentation runs show that the models of high mannose and aggregates at the production bioreactor, selected on the planned runs, did not predict new runs well, and the reports use the models of all runs. After selection `{python} n_none_sel` outputs have no adequate model, and every measured result of these outputs meets its criterion.

The intermediate acceptance criteria in force were fixed at the closure of INV-001 on the selected models. Model selection made `{python} n_cd` of them wider. No conclusion over the NOR depends on the widening, and one proven acceptable range moves at its lower end, outside the NOR. The qualification of the scale-down model for host cell protein in the Protein A pool and at cation exchange does depend on it. The augmentation runs moved no criterion.

At closure the augmentation runs of corrective action CA1 were complete, and the refits of corrective action CA2 and the model selection of corrective action CA3 were complete. The preventive actions were open. INV-002 was closed on `{python} INV2["closed"]`.
